title: The viewer tells of a newer release: Settings → About says the latest release, w
input: The viewer tells of a newer release: Settings → About says the latest release, when it was checked and the channel's command; a dismissible banner at the top says a newer release is out; Settings gains the field for WIZARDINGCODE_MEM_UPDATE (check or off). The viewer only reads what the daily check kept in update.json and never asks the network.

criteria.text: GET /api/update answers the report in the viewer's shape for each state: a release out (the four channels' commands, banner true); the running version the latest; the check off in the file; off by the environment (fromEnvironment true); a value neither check nor off (off-unknown); CI set (ci); not checked yet; a last check that failed; a staged binary of another version gives the agents line; a builder that throws gives 200 with the shape, line saying why, out and banner false and no commands.

POST /api/update/dismiss keeps the release dismissed: banner is false for it afterwards and true again when update.json names a later release; with no release known it keeps nothing; a body that names another version changes nothing of that.

No file of src/ui/ reaches src/update/check.ts through static or dynamic imports, at any depth; and with a check due, answering GET /api/update and POST /api/update/dismiss makes no request to any host but the viewer's own loopback address, counted by a wrapped fetch.

The banner's line, the card's status and tone and the Settings list's mark, as ui/src/update.ts writes them, for each state: out with a staged copy, out with none, latest, ahead, off, off by the environment, off-unknown, not checked in CI, not checked yet, could not check, and a report that could not be built; the About card, the banner over the memories view and the marked list show them at the three widths in both schemes.
The switch's two values go through PUT /api/settings: WIZARDINGCODE_MEM_UPDATE=off and =check are written to the env file, and GET /api/update then says the mode it was set to.

The README says in neither of its two places that WIZARDINGCODE_MEM_UPDATE is set by hand, and says where the viewer tells of a release; CLAUDE.md names the two routes and the files; in docs/real-use/findings.md the row of the missing About line and Settings field says that part is answered, its other remark kept.
tests/integration/ui.test.ts, tests/integration/ui-settings.test.ts and the tests tests/unit/update-boundary.test.ts holds today pass as before.

The other states the page reaches are captured too, at the three widths in both schemes: the running version ahead of the latest release, a value of the key that is neither check nor off, not checked in CI, a report that could not be built, and the banner when no copy is staged.

decisions.question: Where does the viewer show that a newer release is out?
decisions.answer: About + faixa no topo: the About card says the latest release, when it was checked and the channel's command, and a dismissible banner at the top of the viewer says a newer release is out

decisions.question: May the viewer ask github.com for the latest release on a button, or does it only read update.json?
decisions.answer: Só lê (Recomendado): the viewer shows what update.json holds and never asks the network
